title: Cytotoxicity Effect and Bioactive Response of PLGA/PCL/PDO 3D-Printed Leachates Scaffolds Reinforced with Jarosite Doped for Spongy Bone Applications
content: Developing scaffolds with all the necessary mechanical and biological characteristics to mimic cancellous bone and enable its regeneration presents significant challenges. In this work, we leveraged the distinct mechanical properties, elasticity, and degradation kinetics of three distinct polymers. To achieve this, a porogen with a customized internal architecture was produced via 3D printing. A solution containing the blend of the three polymers and jarosite powder was subsequently injected into the printed mold. The porogen structure was then leached away, leaving behind a porous scaffold with the desired internal geometry. This technique enables the fabrication of scaffolds with sinusoidal pores of varying sizes, which facilitate cell viability, proliferation, and nutrient transport. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the synergistic effects of the three-polymer blend, jarosite doping, and a sinusoidal pore morphology on the behavior of human dental pulp mesenchymal stem cells (hDPMSCs). In vitro evaluations demonstrated that the constructed scaffolds are non-toxic, supporting cell viability, migration, and robust proliferation. Furthermore, the bioactive properties of jarosite and its associated ion release actively promote the differentiation of hDPMSCs into osteogenic lineages, demonstrating strong potential for bone tissue engineering applications.
